name: UPWARDS Summer Camp: semiconductors and microelectronics (Virginia Tech)
org: Virginia Tech UPWARDS program and Center for Engineering Excellence and Discovery (CEED)
what_you_do: Spend two weeks in a Virginia Tech residence hall. You do a computer-aided design tutorial. You learn to work safely in a cleanroom. You also build and test simple microelectronic devices.
who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th grade students, per the Virginia Tech engineering pre-college list. The camp pages read do not give more rules.
pay_detail: $2,500 for two weeks. It covers room, board and program costs. You pay your own travel and personal items. Scholarships are available based on financial need. Cancel 30 or more days before camp for a 50% refund.
deadline_text: The program page is out of date. It posts no dates for the next camp, and the apply page still refers to the 2025 application. Call (540) 231-7411 or use the Email UPWARDS link on the page to ask before you apply.
how_to_apply: There are two parts. One is a student application. It has activities, short essays of 120 words or less each, and a transcript. The transcript does not need to be official. The other is a parent form. It has consent and a financial statement used for scholarships. The application is shared with the C-Tech2 camp. You can choose either camp or both.
notes: Costs money and is a camp, not a job. The pages read are partly out of date (they mention the 2025 application), so check the newest page and confirm dates with the program. The Virginia Tech C-Tech2 camp has its own card in this guide.
